note: DRAFT output of a pipeline run outside the medical-insurance domain. Not seeded. Every scenario is fictional and authored from public knowledge.

items.stemAr: A customer opens the call angry about an order that arrived late and broken. What is the first thing you should say?
items.stemEn: A customer opens the call angry about an order that arrived late and broken. What is the first thing you should say?
items.rationaleAr: A person who does not feel heard cannot hear. Acknowledgement names the experience in the customer's words before any cause or fix, and it is not an admission of a fault not yet established.
items.rationaleEn: A person who does not feel heard cannot hear. Acknowledgement names the experience in the customer's words before any cause or fix, and it is not an admission of a fault not yet established.

options.textAr: "I'm sorry you feel that way; let me explain our shipping policy."
options.textEn: "I'm sorry you feel that way; let me explain our shipping policy."
options.feedbackAr: No. This apologises for the feeling rather than the event, then goes straight to defending a policy. The customer hears both as a brush-off.
options.feedbackEn: No. This apologises for the feeling rather than the event, then goes straight to defending a policy. The customer hears both as a brush-off.

options.textAr: "Your order arrived late and broken, and I can see why you are angry."
options.textEn: "Your order arrived late and broken, and I can see why you are angry."
options.feedbackAr: Correct. You named what happened in his words and agreed his experience was bad — a fact he owns — without yet ruling on who was at fault.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. You named what happened in his words and agreed his experience was bad — a fact he owns — without yet ruling on who was at fault.

options.textAr: "I'll transfer you to shipping; they handle deliveries."
options.textEn: "I'll transfer you to shipping; they handle deliveries."
options.feedbackAr: No. Transferring an angry customer before he is heard, and without a handover, makes him explain everything again — which is the road to escalation.
options.feedbackEn: No. Transferring an angry customer before he is heard, and without a handover, makes him explain everything again — which is the road to escalation.

options.textAr: "We'll make it all up to you, don't worry."
options.textEn: "We'll make it all up to you, don't worry."
options.feedbackAr: No. A promise of an outcome whose facts are not yet established and which you may not have authority over. If it does not happen, the complaint becomes about a broken promise.
options.feedbackEn: No. A promise of an outcome whose facts are not yet established and which you may not have authority over. If it does not happen, the complaint becomes about a broken promise.

items.stemAr: You have established the facts and agreed on a refund. Which close is an agreed next step?
items.stemEn: You have established the facts and agreed on a refund. Which close is an agreed next step?
items.rationaleAr: An agreed next step needs three things: a specific action, a specific time, and a way the customer will know it happened. Anything missing one of them sends the customer back to call and create it.
items.rationaleEn: An agreed next step needs three things: a specific action, a specific time, and a way the customer will know it happened. Anything missing one of them sends the customer back to call and create it.

options.textAr: "One of my colleagues will follow up soon."
options.textEn: "One of my colleagues will follow up soon."
options.feedbackAr: No. No name, no time, no way to verify. This is the close that manufactures the repeat complaint.
options.feedbackEn: No. No name, no time, no way to verify. This is the close that manufactures the repeat complaint.

options.textAr: "Done. Is there anything else I can help with?"
options.textEn: "Done. Is there anything else I can help with?"
options.feedbackAr: No. "Done" says neither what was done nor when the customer will see it. Tomorrow he will discover he has no idea whether anything happened.
options.feedbackEn: No. "Done" says neither what was done nor when the customer will see it. Tomorrow he will discover he has no idea whether anything happened.

options.textAr: "I've raised the refund now; it reaches your card within five working days, and you'll get a confirmation email today."
options.textEn: "I've raised the refund now; it reaches your card within five working days, and you'll get a confirmation email today."
options.feedbackAr: Correct. An action, a time, and a way the customer will know it happened — three things he can hold you to.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. An action, a time, and a way the customer will know it happened — three things he can hold you to.

options.textAr: "Email us if the refund doesn't arrive."
options.textEn: "Email us if the refund doesn't arrive."
options.feedbackAr: No. This hands the follow-up burden back to the customer who complained that his email went unanswered. The name on the complaint is yours until it closes.
options.feedbackEn: No. This hands the follow-up burden back to the customer who complained that his email went unanswered. The name on the complaint is yours until it closes.
